Left Behind

Sep 2025A: Analysis

Background

This is a preregistered study, aiming to: (1) establish a basic main effect between feeling left behind and support for candidates endorsing sweeping (as opposed to incremental) change; as well as (2) rule out a positive effect between feeling left behind and support for right-wing candidates.

This was the preregistration:

Hypotheses

  1. Feeling left behind is positively associated with support for sweeping, as opposed to incremental, change.
  2. Feeling left behind is not positively associated with support for right-wing political leaders.

Study design

Participants will first indicate the extent to which they feel left behind.  Then, they will write a brief description of the ways in which they feel left behind, if at all.
Then, they will indicate their preferences for political candidates on the following dimensions: political experience (outsider vs. insider), approach to change (sweeping vs. incremental), and ideological direction (on both economic issues and cultural issues).
Finally, they will indicate their political ideology and party affiliation, as well as their demographic information.

Analysis plan

  1. Linear model 1A: Continuous left behind measure as the predictor variable; preference for political candidate that supports sweeping change as the outcome variable.
  2. Linear model 1B: Continuous left behind measure as the predictor variable; preference for political candidate that supports sweeping change as the outcome variable; race, gender, age, income, and education as control variables.
  3. Linear model 1C: Continuous left behind measure as the predictor variable; preference for political candidate that supports sweeping change as the outcome variable; political party, conservative ideology, progressive ideology, race, gender, age, income, and education as control variables.
  4. Linear model 2A: Continuous left behind measure as the predictor variable; preference for political candidate that supports right-wing policy as the outcome variable.
  5. Linear model 2B: Continuous left behind measure as the predictor variable; preference for political candidate that supports right-wing policy as the outcome variable; race, gender, age, income, and education as control variables.
  6. Linear model 2C: Continuous left behind measure as the predictor variable; preference for political candidate that supports right-wing policy as the outcome variable; political party, conservative ideology, progressive ideology, race, gender, age, income, and education as control variables.

Exploratory analysis

The open-ended text will be coded along the following dimensions, generated with the use of the OpenAI API:
1. The extent of feeling left behind;
2. A list of factors contributing to the feeling of being left behind;
3. The extent to which feeling left behind is due to systemic, as opposed to individual, factors;
4. The extent to which feeling left behind is related to the government;
5. The extent to which feeling left behind is related to economic conditions;
6. The extent to which feeling left behind is related to cultural issues;
7. The extent to which feeling left behind is related to race;
8. The extent to which feeling left behind is related to gender;
9. The extent to which feeling left behind is related to age.
In an exploratory fashion, we will examine these dimensions as moderators for the effects of feeling left behind on preference for political candidates.

Eligibility

There was on bot-check with an invisible attention check.

eligible_n <- df_lebe %>% 
  group_by(is_elg) %>% 
  summarise(n = n()) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  filter(is_elg == 1) %>% 
  select(n) %>% 
  unlist() %>% 
  unname()

df_lebe %>% 
  group_by(att_1) %>% 
  summarise(N = n()) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(Perc = round(100*(N/sum(N)),2)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  kbl() %>% 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "hover",
                full_width = F,
                position = "left")
att_1 N Perc
0 1 0.2
1 499 99.8

That gives us a total of 499 eligible participants.

Participants were recruited through Prolific and the following quota was set for political representativeness: (30% dems; 30% reps; 40% independents)

Politics

Ideology

Participants were asked about the extent to which they subscribe to the following ideologies on a scale of 1-7 (select NA if unfamiliar): Conservatism, Liberalism, Democratic Socialism, Libertarianism, Progressivism.

means <- df_lebe_elg %>%
  dplyr::select(PID,ideo_con:ideo_prog) %>% 
  pivot_longer(-PID,
               names_to = "ideo",
               values_to = "score") %>% 
  filter(!is.na(score)) %>% 
  group_by(ideo) %>% 
  summarise(score = mean(score)) %>% 
  ungroup()

df_lebe_elg %>%
  dplyr::select(PID,ideo_con:ideo_prog) %>% 
  pivot_longer(-PID,
               names_to = "ideo",
               values_to = "score") %>% 
  filter(!is.na(score)) %>%  
  ggplot() +
  geom_density(aes(x = score), fill = "lightblue") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(1,7),
                     breaks = seq(1,7,1)) +
  geom_vline(data = means,mapping = aes(xintercept = score),
             color = "black",
             linetype = "dashed",
             size = 1.1) +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        axis.line = element_line(color = "grey66"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(color = "black"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(color = "black",
                                   face = "bold")) +
  facet_wrap(~ideo,nrow = 2)

Measures

Left behind

Continuous

People in America come from all walks of life. Some feel left behind while others are advancing. We are interested in how you feel and what that means for you.

To what extent do you feel left behind? (0 = Not at All Left Behind to 100 = Extremely Left Behind)

df_lebe_elg %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = lebe_cont)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = "lightblue",
                 binwidth = 5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0,100,20),
                     limits = c(-10,110)) +
  ylab("count") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(df_lebe_elg$lebe_cont,na.rm = T),
             color = "black",

             size = 1.1) +

Open-ended description

IF CONTINUOUS MEASURE < 50

Not everyone feels that they are extremely left behind, but nearly everyone can point to at least a few areas where they feel somewhat left behind…

In what ways, if any, do you feel left behind?

Please describe why you might feel left behind in as much detail as possible. There is no right or wrong answer here; just your honest thoughts about the factors that make you feel left behind.

IF CONTINUOUS MEASURE >= 50

In what ways do you feel left behind?

Please describe why you might feel left behind in as much detail as possible. There is no right or wrong answer here; just your honest thoughts about the factors that make you feel left behind.

85 Social and political issues Well, part of the reason I feel left behind is because of my age. I’m 61. I have the realization that I’m on the back end of my life. When I was younger, I always felt that 60 was so old. Now that I’m that age, while I don’t feel the way I have always interpreted the age of 60 to appear, I feel as though I’m no longer a driving force in this world. But it’s not just my age. The world has changed deeply in my lifetime. The amount of information available has really opened my eyes to the corruption and exploitation that takes place across the globe. I was anti-government for the majority of my life. I didn’t differentiate much between republicans and democrats, though it always seemed to me that democrats were more reasonable and caring than republicans. But over the past 10 years or so, I’ve developed an understanding of how important government is. It’s not that government is bad. It’s that BAD government is bad. We need an ethical and just government to have an ethical and just society. We don’t need smaller government. We need a more just government that helps society, not exploits it for the benefit of the already wealthy. I’ve come to understand what a horrible menace capitalism is. I see how workers are exploited. I grew up thinking that capitalism and democracy goes hand in hand. That you can’t have democracy without capitalism. I now realize that’s a lie perpetrated by wealthy capitalists. I lived the majority of my life trying to do what feels good while dealing with my demons. I mostly accomplished that. I went to college but didn’t graduate. I worked for nearly 30 years as a freelance writer, although I never made very much money. But that allowed me to be a stay-at-home father. I loved that time dearly and have a very close relationship with my child to this day. But the force that I felt that I was (smart, excellent writer, creative, out-of-the-box thinker) – that has dissipated in the past decade. All of my freelance jobs dried up. I no longer was talking to famous musicians and writing award-winning features. I had to go to work outside of the home. I lost my job during the Covid lockdowns. I’ve been unemployed since, other than some freelance work I’ve been able to gather online. I always felt strong, in control of my future. I still feel strong, but I recognize that outside forces control my future more than I do. These are frightening times. The USA has been overtaken by a dictator. Fascism shows its ugly face daily. I shudder at what I see every day. It’s hard to face a future as uncertain as the one I’m facing. I’m scared. It’s the young person’s world now, and I’m no longer a part of that group. You know, for the majority of my life I was the youngest person in whatever group I was with. That’s no longer the case either. Everything just seems so different. I feel left behind.

75 Social and political issues I feel as if the political ideals of the country, primarily those within the upper echelons of it and not the more grassroots elements, have become bastardized to fit the agenda of those with Authoritarian ends. I look to the Democrat Party and I see people who are rapidly devolving into a nightmare of discrimination, identity politics, and an evershifting goalpost used to justify violent rhetoric or violence itself. I look to the Republican Party and I see a heavily fractured party of people having a million different ideas of what “conservatism” looks like, I see people who are stuck in the past trying to re-ignite social issues for personal reasons, and I see the other half of the reason the country has been on a political backslide essentially. Both parties represent to me the failed ideologies that arose within the US after we “won” the Cold War, that being Neoconservatism and Neoliberalism respectively. Both of these ideologies and how they have not only shaped their parties but specifically the Baby Boomer generation have been the architects for some of the worst longterm problems that we face as a nation now, and instead of working to solve some of the problems that are at this point foundational, we instead have the two parties ranting and raving at eachother as their bases become more radicalized to their end of the political spectrum, leaving people who simply want to have a principled opinion in the dust as the rhetoric gets more fiery and the threat of Weimar style political violence gets more and more realized. I guess the best way to put it, even if it’s deeply arrogant, is to simply say that sometimes it feels like the American people are the only sane ones in an insane asylum.

35 Personal growth Of course, this is a very vague thing, being “left behind.” I suppose that could come down to several factors, most of it having to do with feeling that life hasn’t been what you expected it to be. But does that have to do with financial status? Social status? Personal affirmation? It’s hard to say. For me, I feel that I have a robust social life, with many friends of many backgrounds. I have a rich family life, full of laughter and love. I have meaningful spiritual life that nourishes my soul daily. So, in general, I don’t feel “left behind,” yet there is always that nagging feeling that, despite all I’ve accomplished, I could’ve done more by this point. I could’ve published my book. I could’ve produced more music. I could’ve joined a touring band. I could’ve traveled around the globe. I could’ve become a performer. I could’ve become a lawyer, or a doctor. I could be much more rich. I could have way more friends. I could’ve done way more good things for the world. But it’s all conjecture. It’s all a fruitless thought experiment with little bearing in reality. I choose to stay here, in the present, right where I am with what I’m doing and feeling now. And when I realize that my destiny is in the hands of God, and my only job is to be faithful with what He’s given me, then I don’t feel left behind. Feeling left behind means looking back with regret; feeling prideful means looking ahead with lustful ambition; feeling hopeful means being faithful in the here and now.

100 Lack of opportunities Socially, financially and in general, overall. I seem to be lacking in most areas that others have excelled in over recent years, in spite of the pandemic derailing most for a period of time, I never recovered.
30 Social and political issues I’m a white male so from that standpoint this country is not leaving me behind. However, it feels like it is headed in a direction I don’t want to follow. So much hate and division coming from our own government, it makes it hard to live here at times.
60 Career opportunities I largely did everything “right” in terms of growing up. I focused on academics, stayed out of trouble, went to a good college, and interned at a respectable company. However, after graduating I just couldn’t get a full time job in a relevant field. It’s been so long now after graduation that I feel like I’ve lost all desirability in terms of being hired. I’m watching everyone else have fulfilling careers, while I’m just floundering, barely making ends meet.
66 Lack of opportunities I sometimes feel powerless like I don’t have a voice. I know that many people are struggling but it doesn’t make my own struggles any easier. I feel like I don’t have as many opportunities as I imagined in life when I was younger.
18 Inequality and disparity being white means many things are explicitly designed to disadvantage me and my descendants. actually, implicitly as well.
56 Personal growth I’m disabled and haven’t had an opportunity to get married or into a long-term relationship yet. A majority of my contemporaries are married already, so I feel a bit left behind in that sense.
72 Inequality and disparity i feel left behind as a black male because my people are still playing catch up since being freed as slaves and dealing with segregation and racism in america.Wealth is harder to obtain for my people as we didnt and dont really have any generational wealth. the policies being made by the current administration seems to aim to keep black people behind

Systemic


Would you say that the factors that make this person feel left behind are more systemic (larger forces outside their control, like government, society, culture, or the economy) or more individual (their own circumstances and choice)? (1 = entirely individual to 7 = entirely systemic)

df_lebe_elg %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = systemic_gpt)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = "lightblue",
                 binwidth = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1,7,1),
                     limits = c(0,8)) +
  ylab("count") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(df_lebe_elg$systemic_gpt,na.rm = T),
             color = "black",
             linetype = "dashed",
             size = 1.1) +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        axis.line = element_line(color = "grey66"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(color = "black"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(color = "black",
                                   face = "bold"),
        axis.title.x = element_text(color = "black",
                                   face = "bold"))

Cluster analysis

I took the embeddings of the gpt-generated reasons and clustered them using k-means clustering. These are the top-five reasons in each cluster. The label was generated by chat-gpt.

top_examples %>%
  left_join(df_lebe_elg %>% 
              select(cluster,cluster_label) %>% 
              distinct(),by = "cluster") %>% 
  select(-cluster) %>% 
  select(cluster_label,reason,cosine_to_centroid) %>% 
  kbl() %>% 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "hover",
                position = "left") %>% 
  scroll_box(width = "100%", height = "400px")

Then, I wanted to assign a cluster to each participant. So, for each participant, I took the mean of their embeddings, and then took the cosine similarity of that mean with each cluster’s centroid. The highest value is the cluster that the participant was assigned to. Below, I’ll show participants’ assigned cluster, cosine similarity to cluster centroid, and open response.

I’ll also add the mean left behind score for that cluster, just for fun.

df_lebe_elg %>% 
  group_by(cluster_label) %>% 
  summarise(N = n(),
            M_leftbehind = mean(lebe_cont,na.rm = T)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(Perc = round(100*(N/sum(N)),2)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(cluster_label,N,Perc,M_leftbehind) %>% 
  arrange(desc(N)) %>% 
  kbl() %>% 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "hover",
                full_width = F,
                position = "left")
